svg.title: 蜜蜂记账 · 采粉蜂
svg.desc: 奶油黄色底上一只侧身的小蜂，两片翅膀朝后，前足抱着一粒橙红色花粉。
svg.metadata: Initial concept sketch generated with built-in ImageGen. Vector artwork redrawn for small sizes. Create one original, finished app icon design for BeeCount, a welcoming independent personal ledger. Square 1:1 canvas, flat pale warm butter paper background (#FFF0BB), edge to edge to all four corners. Only the symbol. No text, border or drawn app icon tile. Art-direct this like an exceptionally good little character mark printed on the cover of a pocket diary: bold, spontaneous, with presence, at home on an adult's phone. Draw a tiny heavy bumblebee in SIDE PROFILE floating up toward the right, clutching ONE round orange pollen pellet close under its chin, almost like carrying the daily find home. The pellet is a plain small vermilion disk, about a quarter of the width of the bee. Give it an expressive and extraordinarily simple silhouette: plump rounded ink-black rear with a little blunt tail at the lower left, one melted dark round forehead at right, ONE yolk-yellow thick curved band cut through the abdomen. Two large overlapping blunt teardrop wings lean back to the upper left: nearest wing solid warm ivory with clean thick dark outer edge, second a lower ink paddle peeking from behind it. One precise, friendly ivory dot for its eye looking toward the right. Use a single curved black mitten-like foreleg wrapping the pellet, like a little parenthesis. Make the black body one connected, beautifully cut organic mass. A little asymmetry and spring, there is a lot of taste in the few curves. The face has no mouth. Excellent optical balance, simple enough to recognize at 24 px. Center the whole bee including wings and pollen optically with 18 percent margins; no immense empty areas. Hard-edge flat vector style, assured hand-shaped curves, carefully poised proportions, 1950s cut-paper wit with a contemporary independent-app finish. Colors only warm charcoal (#29231F), butter, warm ivory, honey, and the ONE spot of vermilion orange (#EE5834). No gradients, external outlines around everything, fur, hair, paper texture, distressed print, three-dimensionality, glow, drop shadow, legs poking out, long antennae, flight trails, typography, books, coins, currency symbols, letters, shopping bags, or explanatory doodles. Avoid a stock cartoon bee or shiny emoji. Look for an immediately lovable silhouette a person can redraw after one glance.
